`runcheck` requires `admitted − outcomes.keys() == ∅`: missing outcomes mean an undispatched queue. Never put objects in `outcomes`; they fail with exit 2 and a diagnostic directing details to **`outcome_details`**, the optional free-form `{issue-id: object}` map. Store merged heads, reviews, tests, reasons and absorbed epics there. It is absent by default and outside completeness checking; no migration is needed.

The following annotations are additive, outside `runcheck` completeness and do not introduce terminal buckets or require migrations. Issue-id arrays are empty when their condition does not occur. Their distinct Reporting subsections preserve the differences between skipped review, resumable holds, human handoffs and post-merge results.

| Field | Producer and condition | Ledger and reporting meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `discovered_scope_filed` | Count new execution-discovered tickets filed at step 7 (eager L4 build returns), 8.0 (convergence), or 10 (residual/budget-capped scope or opted-out L3 file-and-defer). | New tickets stay outside completeness until admitted to a later build wave. |
| `review_adversarial_skipped` (`[issue-id]`) | During reconciliation, read graft's per-issue `review-verdict.json`: review returned `signal: pass`, `adversarial_outcome: "chain-outage-skipped"` after every backend was unreachable in autonomous mode. Do not change the return-token shape. | These issues shipped without adversarial review. Keep their terminal outcome, normally `shipped`, and identify them separately. Infrastructure outage is not a code defect. |
| `review_outage_pending` (`[issue-id]`) | Graft returned `retry-later` for mandatory-review `unavailable`, with a resumable build-progress checkpoint. | Outcome `parked`, but held for automatic review resume on the next drain, not an ordinary human park. |
| `spec_review_outage_pending` (`[issue-id]`) | Prep returned `spec-review-held` for provider outage. | A never-`admitted` prep hold: no outcome bucket, this array is its sole ledger trace. Use `faff-awaiting-spec-review` and the distinct adversarial-outage subsection. |
| `spec_review_turn_budget_pending` (`[issue-id]`) | Prep returned `spec-review-pending`: healthy but slow fan-out exceeded `prep.spec_review_turn_budget_secs`. | The same never-`admitted` shape and label, but the separate slow-fan-out subsection, never an outage claim. |
| `landing_resumable` (`[issue-id]`) | Append only when graft returns the resumable-hold token after its 25-minute landing budget with a still-open, non-terminal-green PR (CI wait, `BEHIND` rebase churn or settling merge state). Never append for hard-park `pr-open-for-human`. | Outcome `pr-open`. Presence means later landing-loop resume without rebuild; absence means the human handoff, including the hard-parked three-cycle outcome. |
| `post_merge_verification_failures` (`[{issue, pr, merge_sha, command}]`) | At step 11.6, the orchestrator reads shipped issues' `<run-dir>/<issue>/post-merge-verification.json`; never the build subagent writing this array. Add `verified-fail` when merged main HEAD fails its declared `UNIT` re-run. | Keep `shipped`. Per-issue Step 10 already filed the tracker comment and `source: "post-merge"` discovered scope; this is only the run roll-up. Surface separately. |
| `post_merge_verification_unverified` (`[issue-id]`) | Same orchestrator read, for `unverified`: no `UNIT` rung, or worktree/fetch/execution error. | Keep `shipped`. Unprovable is not a defect; nothing else was filed. Surface separately from failed verification. |

- **`declined`** (additive, issue-keyed): `{reason, at, recorded_at}` per routed-out or claimed-by-peer candidate, written only by `faff run-ledger record-declined`; the runner pre-check's `faff drain-filter` skips an issue declined here and unchanged since `at`.
- **`budget`** — the resolved `BudgetEnvelope` plus the `tokens_at_start` baseline, written **once at run start** (alongside the owner stamp): `{ envelope: {ceilings, at_ceiling, price_per_mtok, pricing}, tokens_at_start }`. `faff budget check` reads it each between-units checkpoint; `tokens_at_start` is the run-start transcript-sum so the token dimension counts *this run's* spend, not whole-session history. Absent ⇒ no budget set (every check returns `breached: []`). Informational to `runcheck` — outside the completeness invariant. The envelope's `pricing` field names which rule governs `budget.cost` — always `"map"` (priced per-model × per-class from the built-in map) for a freshly-minted run; `"flat"` only survives on a **legacy** ledger minted before the `budget.price_per_mtok` scalar was removed (its own recorded price/pricing is honoured verbatim so an in-flight run's ceiling never changes mid-run — see `faff budget check`'s docs). When events are token-tagged, this block additionally carries `tokens_at_start_by_class` (the run-start four-class baseline that seeds the per-event checkpoint) and an advancing `tokens_at_last_event` (the last tagged event's cumulative); both are additive telemetry state the CLI maintains — `budget check` still gates on the scalar `tokens_at_start` total, unchanged. A best-effort `tokens_at_start_by_model_class` (per-model baseline, seeded at mint by a lights-out run) additionally sharpens `budget.cost`'s per-model delta under map pricing; its absence (a pre-change ledger) degrades safely to a pro-rated estimate, warned rather than silently wrong.
- **`stop_reason`**: the summary's token, one of `queue-drained`, `all-remaining-parked`, `budget-hit(<dims>)`, `budget-escalated(<dims>)`, `sentry-abort`, `converged/both-dry`, `non-convergence`, `product-incomplete` or `governance-admit-failed`. `faff run close` writes it with the owner close in one locked edit; `run open` writes `governance-admit-failed`, and checkpoint `fail-closed` closes with `sentry-abort`.
